mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES remains near its current depressed level while TRANSIT stays flat, weekday trip chains remain weak and retail visits keep drifting lower over the next four weeks. This is a direct activity shortfall signal, so RETAIL_REC should fall further rather than recover.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES is around -50% and TRANSIT around -60% across the full snapshot window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT do not improve from their current depressed levels.

mechanism_narrative: A further decline in RESIDENTIAL above its recent plateau indicates more time spent at home, which suppresses discretionary shopping trips within one to two weeks. That home-stay shift should push RETAIL_REC lower immediately after the increase in residential presence.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 18 for at least one weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is persistently positive near +17 to +18 while retail stays near -66
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 7 to 14 days after RESIDENTIAL moves above 18, or retail rises despite sustained higher residential time.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise together after a trough, commuting and co-located errands expand with a lag of about two weeks, increasing retail foot traffic. The mechanism predicts a retail rebound only if both series improve at the same time, not if one rises alone.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both series are near their lowest levels in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase within 14 days after simultaneous week-on-week gains in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES, or retail rises when only one of the two improves.

mechanism_narrative: A relative recovery in PARKS should precede higher retail demand within four weeks because outdoor activity supports adjacent spending and weekend trip formation. The effect is conditional on PARKS no longer worsening from its current trough.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stops falling and posts a weekly mean above -45
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declines from -43.3 to -52.1 over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next 28 days even after PARKS rebounds above -45 for at least one weekly mean.

mechanism_narrative: If mobility restrictions tighten enough to suppress TRANSIT further, discretionary retail trips should contract within one week because access friction rises immediately. This is a policy-friction mechanism: the retail series should move lower only after the transit break occurs.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is already near -60 and has not recovered across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 7 days of TRANSIT crossing below -65, or retail rises despite the added transit contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A joint rebound in GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES indicates broader out-of-home activity normalization, and that combination should lift retail over the next two weeks through bundled errand behavior. The claim fails if either series improves without retail responding.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -30 while WORKPLACES rises above -48
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES are both still negative but relatively stable
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after both GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES cross the stated thresholds together.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on persistence effect from the current deep retail slump means that, unless another mobility series sharply improves, retail continues to underperform its recent four-week average. The negative momentum in RETAIL_REC should therefore persist over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC stays around -64 to -67 across all four observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-four-week mean over the next 28 days without a concurrent improvement in other mobility proxies.

mechanism_narrative: In a no-shock regime where TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain pinned near current lows, retail does not recover because commuting-linked shopping opportunities stay suppressed. The next four weeks should therefore keep RETAIL_REC below the prior four-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:transit and workplaces are both deeply negative while residential remains positive
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain near current lows and RESIDENTIAL stays elevated.
